title: Walnut vs HowdyGo vs Storylane Demo Suite (2026)
summary: Walnut vs HowdyGo vs Storylane Demo Suite compared on pricing, setup speed, and CRM depth. Find out which interactive demo platform fits enterprise or self-serve teams in 2026.
body_markdown:
I run marketing at Storylane, so read this knowing I have a horse in the race. But here is my honest take on Walnut vs HowdyGo: neither one is "better."


They are built for two different buyers, and most teams overpay or under-buy because they pick on brand recognition instead of their actual demo scenario. Walnut is the enterprise, AE-led, CRM-wired choice. HowdyGo is the fast, flat-rate, self-serve choice.


This guide maps each to a specific team so you stop comparing feature checklists and start comparing fit.


> **Definition:** An interactive demo platform lets you capture or build a clickable replica of your product, then personalize and share it as a guided tour or embedded experience, so buyers explore your software without a live rep or a sandbox login.


Everything below leans on the buyer language we hear on sales calls: demos that take "forever" to ship, video walkthroughs nobody has time to build, and pricing that feels like guesswork.


## Walnut vs HowdyGo: the quick verdict


Here is the short answer before the detail. Choose Walnut if you are an enterprise or mid-market team running 1:1 personalized demos that must sync to Salesforce and feed revenue attribution. Choose HowdyGo if you are a PLG or marketing team that wants a self-serve interactive demo live this week on a predictable flat budget.


> **Best for at a glance** Walnut: AE-led, CRM-integrated, enterprise-governed demo programs. HowdyGo: fast, flat-rate, HTML-captured self-serve demos for lean teams.


The reason this decision gets muddy is that every ranking page is published by a vendor with a bias, so the "verdict" always bends toward whoever wrote it. My bias is on the table, so I will be blunt about where each tool wins.


If your real goal is passive lead generation through embedded[self-serve demo experiences](https://www.storylane.io/blog/demo-requests) , that scenario points one way; if it is white-glove enterprise selling, it points the other. We will map both.


## Walnut vs HowdyGo at a glance


Before the deep dive, this table lines up the dimensions buyers ask about most: how demos are built, what they cost to start, how long setup takes, and who each tool is really for. Treat pricing rows as reported figures that shift by tier and negotiation, and verify a live quote before you sign.


Two rows deserve early attention. The pricing-model row (per-seat annual versus flat monthly) and the setup row (two weeks versus same-day) are the ones that reshape the decision as your team scales. Read the whole table top to bottom, but weigh those two rows heaviest, because everything else is a supporting detail once they land.

The pattern is consistent: Walnut is the heavier, deeper, pricier platform, and HowdyGo is the lighter, faster, cheaper one. The rest of this guide is about whether that trade lands in your favor.


## Walnut vs HowdyGo pricing compared (real numbers)


Pricing is where this comparison gets decided, and where the web is least honest: one directory page even lists HowdyGo as "Free," which is wrong. So let's put reported numbers on the table.


Walnut runs roughly $6,900 to $9,200 per year at entry (its Ignite tier, around three seats), climbing to roughly $18,600 for Pro or Accelerate, billed annually with no free trial. HowdyGo runs $159 per month flat with unlimited users (about $1,908 per year), a $399 per month Pro tier, and a $99 per month sandbox add-on, with a 14-day trial and no free plan.


The gap is not marginal. At entry, HowdyGo lands between a quarter and a tenth of Walnut's cost, and because HowdyGo is flat while Walnut is per-seat, the divergence widens as teams grow. A cost-per-team-size view makes it concrete.


Team size Walnut (per-seat, annual) HowdyGo (flat)


3 users ~$6,900 (Ignite) $1,908 (Starter)


10 users ~$18,600 (Pro) $1,908


25 users Custom enterprise quote $1,908, $4,788 (Pro)


Buyers are tired of guessing here:


> "Pricing is like the wild west in the space unless it's changed." - a Director of Revenue Enablement & Strategy at a technology company


That is why a team-size pricing view matters more than a headline monthly figure: it lets you compare total cost, not sticker cost. Always confirm current tiers, since published figures move.


## How the demos are actually built


The two tools take different paths to a finished demo, and that mechanism drives almost everything else. HowdyGo uses a no-code Chrome extension to capture your live web app as HTML, producing a pixel-accurate clone you then annotate. Walnut uses a demo builder and personalization wizard, giving more control over branded flows at the cost of more hands-on assembly.


The practical contrast breaks down like this:


- **Fidelity:** HowdyGo's HTML capture mirrors your real UI out of the box, which buyers love for speed. Walnut's builder gives more room to reshape and personalize a flow, which enterprise teams value for tailored 1:1 demos.
- **Editability:** HowdyGo edits are quick but tied to what was captured. Walnut edits are deeper but take longer and lean on a wizard.
- **Maintenance:** Both require re-capturing or rebuilding when your product UI changes, and that upkeep is a real cost buyers underestimate.


That maintenance point is not theoretical. The loudest pain we hear from buyers is that demos are slow and heavy to produce:


> "It's very difficult for us to put together, I would say videos." - a VP of Product Marketing at a enterprise SaaS company


If your team has leaned on manual[product demo and explainer video formats](https://www.storylane.io/blog/saas-product-demo-and-explainer-videos) , both tools are a step up, but they solve the build problem differently: HowdyGo optimizes for shipping fast, Walnut for control.


## Setup time and learning curve


This is the dimension almost no comparison quantifies, and it is often the actual tiebreaker. HowdyGo is a same-day tool: many teams capture and ship a first demo within the first hour.


Walnut is a roughly two-week implementation with a steeper learning curve, because its depth and CRM wiring need configuration. Neither is wrong; they price your time differently.


Buyers raise this first. On one call a marketing leader gated the whole evaluation on it:


> "What's the time to value time to implementation? How quickly can we get going?" - a VP of Product Marketing at a enterprise SaaS company


Here is a simple way to estimate your own time-to-first-demo with each:


1. **Scope one demo.** Pick a single flow you want live, not your whole product.
2. **Capture or build.** HowdyGo: capture the flow via the extension in an afternoon. Walnut: expect configuration plus a build cycle across days.
3. **Annotate and brand.** Add tooltips and steps; both are quick here once the base exists.
4. **Wire the CTA and analytics.** HowdyGo native analytics arrive on Pro; Walnut's CRM sync needs setup but pays off in attribution.


If you need a demo live this week, that sequence favors HowdyGo. If you can absorb two weeks for deeper personalization and CRM data, Walnut earns it.


## Analytics, CRM and integrations


Analytics is where Walnut's extra cost starts to justify itself for revenue teams. Walnut offers deeper Salesforce and CRM flows plus revenue attribution, so demo engagement ties back to pipeline and closed revenue. HowdyGo provides native analytics on its Pro tier and HubSpot or Salesforce connectivity on higher tiers, which covers most SMB and PLG needs.


Use this checklist to decide how much integration depth you actually need:


- **Do you route demo signals into an SDR/AE workflow?** If yes, Walnut's deeper CRM sync earns its keep.
- **Do you need revenue attribution on demo engagement?** Walnut is stronger; HowdyGo covers engagement analytics but less revenue mapping.
- **Is a marketing-owned funnel your main use case?** HowdyGo's native analytics are usually enough.
- **Are you standardizing across**[your sales tech stack](https://www.storylane.io/blog/tools-to-build-the-best-sales-tech-stack) **?** Match the tool's CRM depth to how central demos are to your reporting.


The honest read: many teams buy attribution they never operationalize. If nobody will act on demo-to-pipeline data, you are paying for a Walnut capability you will not use, and HowdyGo's lighter analytics are the smarter fit.


## Support and company profile


The company behind each tool is a real part of the decision, not a footnote. HowdyGo was founded in 2023 in Australia by a small, roughly three-person founder-led team, so support is direct and personal but thinner in scale. Walnut, founded in 2020 in the US, is a larger organization with AE-led support and enterprise governance.


Frame this as a trade, not a knock. A founder-led team often ships fixes fast and answers you directly, but concentration risk is real for a small vendor. A larger org gives procurement-friendly governance and continuity, but you may wait in a support queue and negotiate with sales rather than a founder.


Buyer loyalty in this category is sticky, which cuts both ways when you weigh company profile:


> "We've been a long time walnut user for quite some time at this point. That's our baseline." - a Director of Sales Engineering at a technology company


That kind of incumbency is exactly why switching costs and vendor stability deserve a line in your evaluation, alongside features and price.


## Which tool fits which team? A scenario-based decision guide


Features do not choose a tool; scenarios do. So here are concrete situations mapped to a pick, in both directions, because no single ranking page maps both honestly.


- **An AE running 1:1 personalized demos into Salesforce with attribution:** choose Walnut. The depth and CRM wiring are the whole point.
- **A PLG or marketing team shipping a self-serve interactive demo this week on a flat budget:** choose HowdyGo. Speed and flat pricing win.
- **A services or consulting team that wants a lightweight interactive "skeleton" to spark a sales call:** HowdyGo's speed fits, and this exact motion came straight from a buyer:


> "If we show a basic skeleton of a demo that we have built so they could interact with it and see how it works, even though if it's not in depth, just the basic understanding of it and it might turn into a call or something." - a Business Development Executive at a tech consulting company


- **A product marketer building an always-on website demo hub for passive lead gen:** either tool can embed, but weigh whether you need Walnut's attribution or HowdyGo's speed. One buyer described wanting a "play place" on the site to boost inbound demo requests.
- **A team that needs desktop, mobile, Figma, or video-based demos:** neither is a clean fit; look at[other interactive demo software](https://www.storylane.io/blog/tourial-alternatives) built for those formats.


Write your own scenario in one sentence before you demo either tool. If it names a CRM and personalized selling, that is Walnut; if it names speed, self-serve, and a flat budget, that is HowdyGo.


## Who should NOT pick each tool


The most useful section on any comparison is the one that tells you to walk away. Here are the honest disqualifiers for both.


**Do not pick HowdyGo if:**


- You need deep revenue attribution and enterprise CRM governance today.
- You require desktop, mobile, or non-web app capture; the model is web HTML-first.
- You want a free plan, or you are wary of depending on a small team and a Chrome-extension workflow.
- Your demos need heavy variant personalization at scale.


**Do not pick Walnut if:**


- Budget is tight or unpredictable; per-seat annual pricing scales up fast.
- You need a demo live this week; a two-week implementation will not fit.
- Your use case is simple self-serve tours where enterprise depth is overkill.
- You dislike contract lock-in and want to test before committing, since there is no free trial.


Both lists are real limits, not marketing softeners. If you land on a disqualifier for both, that is a signal to look wider rather than force-fit either tool.


## Where Storylane Demo Suite fits


Full disclosure: this is us, so read it knowing I have skin in the game. Storylane Demo Suite sits between the two poles this article describes. - You want Sandbox Demos that give buyers a live-feeling environment without engineering overhead.
- You need CRM sync and attribution but do not want to commit to Walnut's per-seat annual pricing before you know the ROI.
- A free trial matters: Storylane offers one so you can build and test before committing.


## Bottom line


The Walnut vs HowdyGo decision is not about which platform is objectively best; it is about which one matches your team's motion and budget. Walnut earns its higher price for enterprise, AE-led, CRM-attributed selling. HowdyGo wins on speed, flat pricing, and self-serve simplicity.


If you are still torn, let cost structure break the tie. A per-seat annual tool like Walnut rewards teams that will genuinely use CRM attribution and personalized 1:1 demos, and it punishes teams that buy that depth and never switch it on. A flat tool like HowdyGo rewards teams that value speed and predictable budgets over enterprise reporting.


Write your scenario in one sentence, check it against the disqualifier lists above, and the choice usually makes itself. The buyers who regret this purchase are almost always the ones who bought on brand instead of fit. Match the tool to the motion, not the logo, and you will not overpay for capability you never switch on.


## Frequently asked questions


**Is HowdyGo cheaper than Walnut?** Yes, substantially. HowdyGo's reported entry pricing is around $159 per month flat with unlimited users, while Walnut's entry lands roughly between $6,900 and $9,200 per year for a few seats. Because HowdyGo is flat and Walnut is per-seat, the gap widens as your team grows.


**Does HowdyGo have a free plan?** No. HowdyGo does not offer a free plan, but it does provide a 14-day trial so you can build and test a demo before committing. Walnut offers neither a free plan nor a free trial, so evaluating it means engaging sales.


**Which is better for enterprise?** Walnut, in most cases. Its deeper Salesforce and CRM integration, revenue attribution, and enterprise governance suit AE-led teams with security and process requirements. HowdyGo can serve enterprise marketing teams for self-serve use cases, but it is built lighter.


**Can you migrate demos between them?** Not directly. The two tools build demos differently, HowdyGo through HTML capture and Walnut through its builder, so there is no clean one-click migration. Plan to rebuild key demos if you switch, and factor that rebuild time into your decision.


**Which is faster to set up?** HowdyGo, clearly. Most teams capture and publish a first demo the same day, often within the first hour. Walnut typically takes around two weeks to implement because of its depth and CRM configuration.
